title: Crossing the Gender Binary: Modelling Gendered Reference in Science Fiction and General Fiction
abstract: arXiv:2610.19028v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Science fiction is widely credited with unsettling gender. This article asks whether that holds at the linguistic level, in how readily gendered reference gives way to its counterpart, a neutral term, or other social category, and whether it separates the genre from general fiction. It does so by masking man/men, woman/women, and person/people across same-period science fiction and general fiction corpora and classifying RoBERTa's five likeliest substitutes by gender. Retention and displacement are permutation-tested over five resampling rounds, and the underlying sentences are read closely. Both corpora cross the gender binary in both directions, but unequally: where woman is masked, the model predicts a masculine term about twice as often as it predicts a feminine term where man is masked. translated_title: 跨越性别二元：科幻小说与一般小说中性别化指称的建模研究
translated_abstract: 科幻小说被广泛认为具有撼动性别观念的力量。本文探讨这种力量是否在语言层面成立，即性别化指称在多大程度上容易让位于中性词或其他社会类别，以及这是否使科幻小说区别于一般小说。研究方法是在同期的科幻小说与一般小说语料库中遮蔽 man/men、woman/women 和 person/people，并按性别对 RoBERTa 预测的五个最可能的替代词进行分类。保留与替代情况经过五轮重采样的置换检验，并对相关句子进行了细读分析。结果显示，两个语料库都以双向方式跨越了性别二元，但存在不平等：当遮蔽 woman 时，模型预测出阳性词的频率约为遮蔽 man 时预测出阴性词频率的两倍。每一次不匹配都代表一个统计学上的意外——一个语料库没有预料到会出现在该位置的词。与这一共同模式相比，科幻小说表现出更大的性别……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究通过遮蔽性别词并利用 RoBERTa 对替代词进行建模，发现科幻小说与一般小说在语言层面均存在双向跨越性别二元的指称现象，但具有不对称性——woman 被遮蔽时更易被阳性词替代——而科幻小说在这一共同模式之上展现出更大的性别灵活性。
en_tdlr: Using masked-language modelling with RoBERTa, this study reveals that both science fiction and general fiction cross the gender binary in gendered reference asymmetrically, with science fiction exhibiting greater gender flexibility than general fiction.
